title: Photos reveal The Smiths' 'dramatic' Manchester farewell

input.lead: Rarely-seen images from what proved to be the iconic band's penultimate show surface 40 years on
input.summary: Rarely-seen images from what proved to be the iconic band's penultimate show surface 40 years on
input.evidence_text: Manchester's Free Trade Hall has a special place in music history, as the venue - now a hotel - hosted some landmark moments It was where an electric guitar-wielding Bob Dylan famously faced an accusation of "Judas!" from a disgruntled folk fan , where a Sex Pistols show that inspired some of the city's most famous bands and the legendary Factory Records and where rock giants Kiss made their UK debut And it was where The Smiths, one of Manchester's most iconic bands, played what would prove to be their final farewell to the city on 30 October 1986 Forty years on, rarely-seen photos of the show, taken by then-student Alison Bell show what she said was a "dramatic" and "amazing" night Bell, who had been drawn to Manchester by its music scene as a student and went on to have a successful career in music promotion, said she had been desperate to see the band and the Free Trade Hall show was "the first opportunity I had to see them" Formed by singer Morrissey and guitarist Johnny Marr in 1982, the band were at the peak of their powers at the show, riding high on the success of their third long-player, The Queen Is Dead, which would go on to become widely-regarded as one of the greatest albums of all time

title: Oldham: Murder suspect faces investigation over five burglaries

input.lead: A man in his 70s was found dead during a search of an address on Whitstable Close
input.summary: A man in his 70s was found dead during a search of an address on Whitstable Close
input.evidence_text: A man has been arrested on suspicion of murder while already being investigated over five aggravated burglaries, Greater Manchester Police has said A man in his 70s was found dead during a search of an address on Whitstable Close, in Chadderton, Oldham He is believed to have died between 4 and 7 November, with his death being treated as suspicious. His loved ones have been informed A man in his 30s has been arrested on suspicion of aggravated burglary and murder, and remains in custody for questioning He had already been arrested in relation to five aggravated burglaries between January and October when detectives linked him to the murder case The victims in the burglaries had all been targeted similarly, with the suspect attempting to or gaining entry to their properties before demanding they hand over their bank cards and pin codes, the force said

title: How property, football and politics link Manchester and Abu Dhabi

input.lead: A closer look at the relationship between Man City's owners and the Manchester political scene
input.summary: A closer look at the relationship between Man City's owners and the Manchester political scene
input.evidence_text: When Manchester City was found guilty in September of breaching Premier League financial rules, the damning and unprecedented verdict left the football world reeling An independent commission said the club had "systematically" broken rules between 2009 and 2018 by inflating sponsorship revenue to disguise secret funding of more than £830m into its football operations Speculation is now rife about the level of punishment City will face, although the club denies any wrongdoing and has appealed against the ruling While we await the outcome, the historical relationship between City's Abu Dhabi-based owners and Manchester's political elite - including the now Prime Minister Andy Burnham - has been in the spotlight There has been a focus on land deals, multimillion-pound regeneration schemes, and more recently, investigations into loans handed out to property companies owned ultimately by City's owner, the Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG) Beyond the on-field success at the Eithad Stadium, what exactly is the Abu Dhabi story in Manchester?

input.summary: Greater Manchester Police say a man, in his 60s, died in the fire in Middleton on Saturday afternoon

title: The case against each man accused of abusing woman drugged by husband

input.lead: The prosecution has been outlining its case against nine men accused of abusing an unconscious woman
input.summary: The prosecution has been outlining its case against nine men accused of abusing an unconscious woman
input.evidence_text: This past week prosecutors have been outlining their case against a group of nine men - including a paramedic, children's football coach and taxi driver - who allegedly raped or abused a woman after she had been drugged by her husband The husband, who cannot be named to protect his wife's legal right to anonymity, had already pleaded guilty to 62 offences against her committed at the home they shared in the Stockport area of Greater Manchester Four other men have also admitted sexual offences against her, but the remaining defendants deny all charges and are on trial at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court Louise Oakley KC, lead counsel for the prosecution, has told the jury that both the husband and the other men were leading "double lives" while secretly fulfilling their "barbaric fantasies" The husband's own abuse against the woman, in her sixties, is believed to have begun in 2004 before he began inviting strangers he met on online chatrooms, swinging websites and messaging apps to join him from about 2023 Here the BBC summarises the allegations against each man standing trial

input.summary: Robert Smethurst was released without further action after a thorough investigation, Cheshire Police says

title: Salford man's journey from brain injury to stand-up comedy

input.lead: Ben Shelvin was once told he would never talk or walk ever again but found a unique way to bounce back
input.summary: Ben Shelvin was once told he would never talk or walk ever again but found a unique way to bounce back
input.evidence_text: A man who was once told he might never walk or talk again following a devastating brain injury says stand-up comedy has become the key to his recovery Ben Shelvin was hospitalised after a drunk driver crashed into his moped during a family holiday to Croatia back in 2003 Now aged 44, Shelvin, from Salford, has made a near complete recovery, and has gone on to carve out a career performing stand-up comedy, and even run half-marathons He described the road to recovery as "a long process" but said the best advice he had to offer was to "just keep going" Born in 1982, Shelvin said his childhood was very active, and filled with all kinds of sport, including football, athletics, and cricket He went on to study at Manchester Metropolitan University, and the day after his graduation flew out to Dubrovnik in Croatia for a two-week family holiday

input.evidence_text: After spending more than 20 years living in caravans and motorhomes, army veteran James Makinson said having a permanent home gave him one thing: "security" Known as Jimmy, the 79-year-old was helped into accommodation in Wigan through Homes at Ease, a housing programme run by the not-for-profit organisation Armed Forces Community HQ The scheme helps veterans who are homeless or at risk of losing their homes find permanent accommodation through social housing providers and private landlords. Since 2023, it has received more than 500 referrals across the North West "I can't say enough about this place," Makinson said of Armed Forces Community HQ, which helped him Lisa Murgatroyd, strategic development director at the organisation, said 99.5% of veterans housed through the scheme remained in permanent accommodation for more than six months Murgatroyd said much of the homelessness experienced by veterans was hidden, with people staying on friends' sofas or in insecure accommodation rather than sleeping rough

View 6 Images Eccles Add to preferred sources News Charlotte Hall Local Democracy Reporter 16:40, 08 Nov 2026 It’s just past 4PM on a Thursday in Eccles, and people are fighting in the street. A brawl spills out onto the pavement outside a pub, and a drunk man is headbutted to the ground City Mayor Paul Dennett attempts to intervene. He’s out on a ‘walkabout’ with the M.E.N. and ward councillor and deputy mayor coun Mike McCusker to discuss the upcoming regeneration of Eccles town centre. It’s a major 15-year multi-billion-pound plan that could completely rejuven “So, there are some problems with anti-social behaviour around here,” coun McCusker says, deadpan, as we watch the city mayor pick the bleeding man off the floor. “The plan is to change that, too.” View 6 Images Councillor Mike McCusker (left) and City Mayor Paul Dennett (right) in Eccles town centre The project, which is due to be approved by council bosses at a cabinet meeting next week, includes new green and community spaces, and 1,300 new homes across a number of low and mid-rise buildings, alongside a smaller number of tower blocks up to 12 storeys high

Using sculpture, installation, film, photography In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. But music has always been part of his story, and since launching his career as KVDZ in 2022, he’s been steadily building a catalogue of deeply pe His debut release Caution, a collaboration with Smila, was followed by his first solo single 8th Floor, produced by Freddie Mines and inspired by his experiences growing up in East London. input.evidence_text: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities. The government has published its D The plan acknowledges that the challenge is not simply a shortage of people with digital skills. Entry-level recruitment has become more difficult, with employers increasingly favouring experienced candidates and many graduates and other new entrants struggling to secure their fi Manchester Digital contributed to the development of the plan through its involvement in the government's Digital Skills Council, drawing on its work with employers and education providers across Greater Manchester Around 800,000 digital and technology roles are projected to need filling over the next decade. The plan sets out an ambition to create 200,000 entry-level jobs, including apprenticeships, during that period The plan also addresses how AI is changing workforce requirements and the importance of ensuring people entering the industry have both technical knowledge and practical workplace skills Manchester Digital's 2026 Sector Insights Report highlighted a reduction of around 20% in early-career opportunities, despite continued demand for experienced technology professionals

That depends who you ask… Tech by Chris Newbould November 4, 2026 Lecturers and students have significantly different perceptions of how much generative artificial intelligence (AI) is being used in university studies, according to new research from The University of Manchester and Spain’s Universidad del Pais Vasco/Euskal Herriko Unibertsitatea. The study found that academic staff perceived students to be using AI tools such as ChatGPT for their studies much more extensively than students reported themselves. Researchers say the findings highlight a gap in understanding between staff and students, at a time when universities are grappling with how best to respond to the technology. Academic staff rated their perception of students’ AI use at 5.23 out of seven, compared with an average of 3.11 among students reporting their own use for academic purposes. The most prominent uses reported by students involved producing written text, finding answers to assignments, and translating or improving grammar. Staff varied considerably in their experience and expertise with AI, making it difficult for some to judge how students were using the technology. Crediflow AI has developed a platform that pulls together the information credit teams currently gather and process by hand, such as financial statements, bank transactions and borrower documents, and turns it into structured credit analysis. input.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained.
